evals.prompt: Here's our signup form in React: email and password inputs with placeholder text as labels, errors shown on every keystroke, the submit button disabled until everything is valid, and the form resets if the API returns an error. Fix it.
evals.expected_output: Adds visible labels, moves validation to on-blur then on-input after an error, keeps submit enabled and focuses the first invalid field on submit, preserves input on API errors with a specific message, adds type/autocomplete attributes, a loading state with unchanged label and double-submit protection.
expectations: Every input gets a visible label; placeholder is not used as the label
Validation first runs on blur (not on the first keystroke) and clears as soon as the value becomes valid
Submit button is not pre-disabled; on submit the first invalid field receives focus
Entered values are preserved when the API returns an error
Email input uses type=email and autocomplete (email or username); password uses autocomplete new-password or current-password
Submit shows a loading state and prevents double submission

evals.prompt: Users can delete tasks from a list. Right now it opens a modal 'Are you sure? Yes / No'. Can you improve this?
evals.expected_output: Replaces the confirmation with immediate soft-delete plus an Undo toast (~5–10 s, pausing on hover/focus), keyboard-reachable Undo, hard-delete after the window; if a confirmation is kept for bulk or irreversible cases, uses specific verb buttons.
expectations: Recommends Undo instead of a confirmation dialog for this reversible action
Undo is offered for a bounded window of several seconds
Implementation soft-deletes first and permanently deletes only after the window
Does not use 'Yes' / 'No' as button labels anywhere in the solution

evals.prompt: In our admin app, clicking a customer row opens a modal with the customer's details and an edit form with 20 fields; from there 'View invoices' opens another modal. What's a better pattern?
evals.expected_output: Moves detail/edit into a side sheet or a full page with a URL, eliminates modal-on-modal by navigating or replacing content, keeps list context, restores focus, and makes the open item deep-linkable.
expectations: Replaces the modal with a side sheet/drawer or a dedicated page
Explicitly removes the modal-on-modal (nested modal) pattern
Makes the open customer (and invoices view) addressable by URL so Back and sharing work
Mentions focus handling on open and close

evals.prompt: Our data table with 50,000 rows is slow to scroll and sorting takes seconds. How do we fix it?
evals.expected_output: Near-miss: this is a data-dense UI and performance problem (virtualization, server-side sorting/pagination) owned by data-dense-ui; a good answer addresses virtualization or server-side operations rather than only interaction states or copy.
expectations: Does not limit the answer to loading spinners or microcopy changes
